utterances.text: They said his name Ajet Gashi; that he had been a security inspector of Serbia; that in the 1990s he had left his job, like all of the other Albanian policemen and inspectors; and that after that indirectly he had been working for the Serb forces in Lipjan; that he had done some bad things. This is what rumour said. And I was certain that that was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, when you went to that room and you saw the three or four persons, did you -- did you know which of the three -- whether Ajet Gashi was in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. For him I was there. I wanted to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And which one was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was the person that Ymer had turned to, the person that couldn't stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did Ymer say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall. But when he opened the door he said something, a provocative word, Where are you spies, or something like this. I'm not certain about his exact words.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I said, Let's go. I think he wanted to stay there more. I was afraid he might strike someone there and so I said, Let's go. We were at the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go after you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Court what other occasions you had to see either of those two rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that occasion, I said I am not sure. Then later I know that there were prisoners in both rooms, in both those rooms. There were some Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. others who were not in those two rooms whom I met outside those two rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: For the moment I want to focus on those two rooms. Can you remember other times that you went and saw prisoners in those two rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Went there again, but later. I don't remember when, but I know that I went maybe once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On those other occasions what did you see? Can you describe what you saw in those rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the second occasion I think I went to look for someone. I went there, I'm not sure with whom I went - I think it was Ymer - there was a greater number of people there. On the second occasion I know that the number of people was greater. There was a stench in the room when the door was opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you observe -- you said there was a -- a greater number of people. What -- did you observe anything about those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this occasion, I think one of them was chained because behind his back I saw some chains. The chains were there from before; they were used for animals. And I know that I asked one of them who was standing by the door. I asked him what was his name. And he told me his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, we're in public session so I would ask you to be careful about mentioning names. Can you describe -- on these other occasions when you went to these two rooms in the prison compound, can you describe the condition of the prisoners. How did they appear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On all the occasions I have been there to those rooms, there was always someone who seemed to have been maltreated, beaten up, injured. Not all, but some of them. And the situation there was grave. It smelled. It had a very bad smell. Maybe because it was overcrowded, maybe because it was used to keep animals there. That's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that some -- some appeared to have been maltreated. Can you describe any of the injuries that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In one occasion I remember someone had scars or bruises on his face. I -- I saw it with my own eyes. In another occasion, I saw a person who was really badly injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten up. You could see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Had a could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had signs, bruises, on his face, bruises that came from beating. Probably there were bloodstains on his face. I don't know about his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you know how people ended up in that prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. These people were arrested. They were brought there to Lapusnik. They were arrested in different places, not in Lapusnik. I don't know who arrested them, whether it was our unit, but they were arrested in Blinaje, in Kroimire, and in other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know why they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The rumours were that all of them were arrested for collaborating with the Serb power, with the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said "the rumours." What did you mean about that? How did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- there were words. Because nobody was arrested for being good. They were arrested either for having worked with the Serb government, or they were suspected of continuing to work with them in the 1980s and in the 1990s. In the 1990s it was very difficult in Kosova. For a word, you could end up in gaol and get a sentence of 15 years, just for saying Kosova republic, or if you were suspected of having a weapon. You could end up in trouble. I believe that those who rendered a direct contribution to that situation in Pristina or other places, they were the ones who ended up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know if the people who were arrested were Albanian, Serbs or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them were Albanians, with the exception of one case when there were two Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll ask you more about that case later. Do you know what would happen when these people who were arrested were brought to Lapusnik? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that often they were brought there beaten. On the place where they were arrested they were beaten up and when they were brought to Lapusnik they were beaten up and maltreated. Some, for example who were arrested in Blinaje, one or two, when they were brought to Lapusnik, they were in a very bad state.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard from the soldiers that after they were arrested, they were beaten. Badly beaten and very late that day or on the next day they were brought to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know whether these people who were arrested were ever questioned in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think so, yes. They were questioned. Because there were some who went there to question them. They were given a notebook. I say it in one instance, where he wrote in that notebook what he had done, with whom he had collaborated and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know anything about who would make these arrests, who would actually arrest these people and bring them to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The army arrested them or there was some note with reference to that person and if he showed up somewhere where the guards were, the guards of the KLA, he would end up arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who had the authority to arrest people? Did any soldier have authority to arrest somebody and bring him to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Soldiers who were on guard, they either had a list -- usually they had a list of wanted persons and if that person was on that list, they would certainly be detained. Or most of them the soldiers knew because they were from the same place. In some cases had happened like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know if Qerqiz had any role or responsibility with regard to the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if that Qerqiz has arrested someone or that he has given orders to arrest someone. But in the prison, he could enter and he has entered. This I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see him enter the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two or three times. Maybe two times for sure I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him entering the prison? Were you inside the prison, outside the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was outside. I was never inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you see him enter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into the door that was on the opposite side where that house -- where the kitchen was. I saw him entering that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever see Qerqiz wearing a mask?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once, when he left the prison. And when he came outside, he took off the mask. It was the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. The translation is little -- either the answer or the translation is a little unclear it says that -- the answer that we got that you saw him wearing a mask "when he left the prison. And when he came outside, he took off the mask." Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you say him wearing the mask was he going into the prison or coming out of the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was leaving the prison. He was coming out of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay, that's clear now. Did you ever see Celiku in the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever see him on the road outside of the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the cars. That was the road where the cars came from, to go to the prison and to the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you saw the cars can you tell us what cars you saw? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually it was a Jeep, a Jeep that you drove, or that he came with. I don't remember to have seen any other car other than that Jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you saw the car on the road outside the prison, was anybody in the car or -- or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But I wasn't at the car, but on the basis of what we said, who was coming, then I understood that it was Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was the car moving or was it parked when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In one instance I saw the car as it was coming. In another occasion, I saw the car parked between the prison and the kitchen. In that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on the occasion that you saw the car parked, whose car did you think it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew -- I knew whose car it was. But I told you that I didn't see him entering the prison. Maybe he has used the other side where the kitchen and the oda was. But from the others I heard that Celiku had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever see Qerqiz in the compound across the road from the prison, the one that was used for a kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the yard of the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, in the yard of the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of us stayed there because we went there to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did all of us include Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Qerqizi and everybody was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever Celiku in that compound, the yard of the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure about the time, but in July I know that I saw him up, upstairs. I don't think I have seen him at the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you mean by you say "upstairs"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean the place where the headquarters and the clinic, that small clinic were. There was a yard in front. There was a big oda, that big room. In that room I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that a different place from the compound where the kitchen was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's some 200 metres from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you again on the computer monitor an image from P005 and the building A1 and the gate. Do you see that on the computer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: First of all, was that building there that we can see, it's A1, was that ever used by soldiers for social gatherings during the time that you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on the image that you see in front of you, can you see -- did you see Shala on any -- on this part of the compound that is depicted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, near the door. And on this balcony or terrace here, where the steps are, that go up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you say near the door, which door are you referring to, if you could describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main gate, the large metal gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, when did you first hear about this person when you were at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe on the day he was stopped or the next day. I believe it was the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember what month that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember correctly if it was the end of May or early June, the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know how he was stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards had stopped him near position number three. He had brought a generator in Lapusnik. He was stopped and taken to a house near position number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did he get to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came in a Lada vehicle. And his Lada remained there until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Remained where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was like a sports field near position number 3. The place where he was stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you know this had happened to this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first day, when he was questioned he had mentioned many names. He was asked about collaborators and he had mentioned many names. He said for his own village that all of the persons from his village were spies. Amongst these names he had mentioned my name as well and said that I had helped some people who regulate some documents. This was it. Qerqiz told me about this, and I went with him to see him. He had said that he knows me very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go to see this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Lagjja e Sopaj, or the Sopaj neighbourhood. It is near Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. position number 3. It was an oda. He was there inside. He had a notebook in his hands, and he had written a page or two in his notebook. This is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, do you know why this person was stopped in the first place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was accused of collaborating with some Serb policemen and for completing some work for them. And the generator that he had brought, we were suspicious that the Serb forces might have planted something in the generator and that is why it was suspicious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know when he was questioned if he ever admitted to being a collaborator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened when you went to see this person with Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was writing in a notebook, and he didn't feel that he was arrested. He felt as if he was free. He was alone in that room. I asked him about a person that he mentioned, whether he knows him and he said yes. I again asked, Do you know him. He said, Yes I know him very well. Then I again asked, If he had a beard would you still know him? And he said, Yes, even if his beard is half a metre long I would still recognise him. Qerqiz didn't let me deal with him. We left. We went outside. He just told him to continue with his writing and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that Qerqiz wouldn't let you deal with him, this person. And again please don't use his name. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wanted to say that I would probably have stayed there longer with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, how would you have dealt with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If he continued in that direction about what he said about many people, about many villages, I'm sure I would have beaten him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how did Qerqiz prevent you from dealing with him? What did you do to prevent you from dealing with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, Let him write down [as interpreted] and we will come here again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see this person again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went again to the same place. However, something happened at the door. I again went there with Qerqiz. But we did not go inside. We just went to the door. We didn't speak with him. When I heard that he was in prison, in the prison, then I looked for him in the prison. But I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you hear that he was in the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And why did you try to go see him in the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had spoken about many names, and I wanted to continue my conversation with him. And as I said earlier, I wanted to beat him, if he pursued in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you've testified already that you went in fact to the prison that you have identified with photographs. Is it your testimony that you didn't -- did not see him there at the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know if this person ever admitted to being a collaborator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if he admitted. But surely, if he spoke ill of so many others, he could have said something like that for himself. Some from his family came to look for him. I know that he is alive and I know that he was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know when he was released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was released in the end of July. This is what I think. Because up to July people asked for him. He was released sometime in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember who asked -- who came from his family came to ask for him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His wife and another female came once. I don't know if she -- the other female was his sister. And on the other occasion, his uncle came. He was a man in his 40s or 50 he is. He introduced himself as his uncle and said he was looking for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you talk to the uncle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I met him accidentally and I spoke with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you tell him about where this person was that he was looking for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told him that I didn't know where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you say it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I wasn't the person who could release him or deal with him, and that's why -- why should I give information about his whereabouts. And, on the other hand, I was not sure whether he was still in the location where I saw him. Therefore, it was better for me to say that he wasn't there and that I would ask where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know who spoke with his wife when she came to look for him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that she went to Qerqiz. I don't know whether she went to speak with him and if she met him. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another case, and this is about Ajet Gashi. You testified that the first time that you went to the prison compound was to see this person Ajet Gashi. Can you tell us again about what you heard about why Ajet Gashi had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was said that Ajet Gashi and one or two of his brothers had set off for one of the staffs, that he went to one of these staffs and brought some weapons to them and asked to join the KLA. His brothers returned because they were told that there wasn't a need for all of them, while Ajet was kept there. I don't know when he was arrested, whether he was arrested later or then when he was stopped. I don't know that. And as I mentioned earlier it was believed that he was a spy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you know if he was questioned or interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that there were rumours about an incident when a student, Albanian student, female student during the demonstrations in Kosova and she was interrogated by Ajet Gashi to maltreated her in different ways. It was said that this student identified Ajet as Ajet Gashi as a person who perpetrated those actions and that Ajet Gashi admitted to have committed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, how did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everything was spoken between the soldiers. We weren't a lot there. In conversation with soldiers, with people, who were in uniforms. I don't know from whom, but this is what was said and everybody knew about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was anything -- did you hear anything about whether he admitted to being a spy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I heard that he admitted everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood him to be a collaborator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you hear any other information about how he was a collaborator or what he had admitted to or -- or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where he came from. Not even today. I don't know where he comes from. What I now is that for sometime he had lived in Lipjan and it is then when he was believed to have collaborated with the Serb forces. And it was said that he illegally received a salary for collaboration with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when was that? At the time that he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's in the 1990s. Up to the time when he was arrested. I don't know about the time, just about the time he was arrested, but until then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, did you hear anything about any other information that Ajet Gashi was said to have provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had given the name of another person, that that person was also a spy; this is what I heard. And I knew the person whose name he had given.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, you said that -- that you went twice to arrest this person. Why did you go twice to arrest this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, there was information about him, that he was a collaborator, and this was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you go on your own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the first occasion, I went alone, but I met with several other soldiers who had gone there before in my house. And on the second occasion, we went together. Altogether we were five. But we didn't reach the destination. We lost our ways in the mountains and as it was already getting early in the morning we returned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who decided that this person should be arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I said that Qerqiz asked me, that Ymer told me. However, Ymer went there to arrest him with some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But when you went to try to arrest him was it your decision or was it somebody else's decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was Ymer's decision. He called me. We got in the vehicle and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning when this case will continue. So if you could return for your evidence to continue at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Thank you. We adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
